text: When two men have a dispute, they shall come before the court, and the judges shall decide between them, acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty.
If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime deserves.
He may be given forty lashes, but no more; otherwise, if he is beaten beyond this with many blows, your brother will be degraded in your sight.
You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

If brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, the widow of the dead man shall not marry outside the family. Her husband's brother shall take her as his wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law to her.
The first son she bears shall carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name is not blotted out of Israel.

But if the man refuses to take his brother's widow, she shall go up to the elders at the city gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to preserve his brother's name in Israel; he will not do his duty as a brother-in-law to me."
Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak with him. If he stands his ground and says, "I do not want to take her,"

his brother's widow shall step up to him in the presence of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and declare, "So shall it be done to the man who will not build up his brother's house."

versions.text: his brother's widow shall go up to him in the presence of the elders, pull the sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and declare, "This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's house."
versions.explanation: The verb here is נגש (draw near/approach), not עלה (go up), which was used in verse 7 for going up to the gate. Using "go up" again blurs the distinction; "step up to him" keeps the movement natural for oral reading while reflecting the different verb.

versions.text: his brother's widow shall step up to him in the presence of the elders, pull the sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and declare, "This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's house."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the possessive suffix on נַעֲלוֹ ("his sandal"), which the definite "the sandal" flattens; keeping the possessive also strengthens the link to verse 10's "the house of the man whose sandal was pulled off." The imperfect יֵעָשֶׂה is prescriptive ("so shall it be done"), a declaration of the standing penalty rather than a report of custom, and the imperative rhythm reads well aloud.

text: And his family shall be known in Israel as "the house of the man whose sandal was pulled off."

If two men are fighting with each other, a man and his countryman, and the wife of one comes to rescue her husband from the man who is beating him, and she reaches out her hand and seizes him by his private parts,

versions.text: If two men are fighting and the wife of one comes to rescue her husband from the man who is beating him, and she reaches out her hand and seizes him by his private parts,
versions.explanation: The phrase אִישׁ וְאָחִיו ("a man and his brother/countryman") is omitted. It signals that the brawl is between fellow Israelites, which matters for the severity of the following penalty.

text: you shall cut off her hand; show her no pity.
You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one large and one small.

versions.text: You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew pair גְּדוֹלָה וּקְטַנָּה is the same expression used in verse 14 ("large and small"). Rendering it identically preserves the deliberate parallelism between the two verses, which is especially effective when read aloud.

text: You shall not have two differing measures in your house, one large and one small.
You shall have an accurate and honest weight, and an accurate and honest measure, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
For everyone who does such things, everyone who deals dishonestly, is detestable to the LORD your God.
Remember what the Amalekites did to you along the way when you came out of Egypt:
how they met you on the road and cut down all who were straggling behind, when you were weary and worn out; they had no fear of God.

Therefore, when the LORD your God gives you rest from all the enemies around you in the land he is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!
